paragraphs: Amazon.com, Inc. (doing business as Amazon) is an American multinational conglomerate engaged in e-commerce, retail, cloud computing, online advertising, digital streaming, entertainment, and artificial intelligence. Founded in 1994 by Jeff Bezos in Bellevue, Washington, the company started as an online book marketplace that gradually expanded to include virtually all consumer products as well as many other categories, positioned as "The Everything Store".
As of 2026 it was the world's biggest online retailer. Amazon sells books, electronics, pharmaceuticals, car parts, video games, dining products, jewelry, food, music, and sports equipment.

The company has multiple subsidiaries, including Amazon Web Services (AWS), which provides cloud computing; Zoox, a self-driving car division; satellite Internet provider Kuiper Systems; and Amazon Lab126, a computer hardware R&D provider. Other subsidiaries include Ring, Twitch, IMDb, and grocer Whole Foods Market. Amazon distributes downloadable and streaming content through its Amazon Prime Video, MGM+, Amazon Music, Twitch, Audible, and Wondery units through its Entertainment division. It publishes books through its publishing arm, Amazon Publishing; produces and distributes film and television content through Amazon MGM Studios, including the Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer studio; and owns Brilliance Audio and Audible, which produce and distribute audiobooks, respectively. Amazon produces consumer electronics, most notably Kindle e-readers, Echo devices, Fire tablets, and Fire TVs.

Amazon has a reputation as an industry disruptor through innovation and aggressive reinvestment of profits. As of 2023, it was the largest online retailer and marketplace, smart speaker provider, cloud computing service provider through AWS, live-streaming service provider through Twitch, and Internet company as measured by revenue and market share. In 2021, it surpassed Walmart as the world's largest retailer outside of China, supported by its subscription plan, Amazon Prime, which had 200 million subscribers worldwide. It is the second-largest private employer in the US, second-largest company in the US by revenue as of 2024 (after Walmart), and the largest company in the world by revenue as of 2026. As of October 2024, Amazon was the world's 12th-most visited website. 84% of its traffic comes from the US.

Amazon has been criticized for its alleged business practices, including surveillance partnerships, poor working conditions, anti-union efforts, environmental harm, anticompetitive behavior, censorship controversies, and exploitative treatment of small businesses and suppliers.

people.name: Jeffrey P. Bezos
people.title: Executive Chair
people.bio: Founded Amazon.com in 1994 and has served as Chair of the Board since 1994. Served as Chief Executive Officer from May 1996 until July 2021, when he became Executive Chair.
people.quote: Jeffrey P. Bezos. Mr. Bezos founded Amazon.com in 1994 and has served as Executive Chair since July 2021.

people.name: Andrew R. Jassy
people.title: President and Chief Executive Officer
people.bio: Has served as President and Chief Executive Officer since July 2021. Previously served as CEO Amazon Web Services from April 2016 until July 2021 and Senior Vice President, Amazon Web Services, from April 2006 until April 2016.
people.quote: Andrew R. Jassy. Mr. Jassy has served as President and Chief Executive Officer since July 2021

people.name: Matthew S. Garman
people.title: CEO Amazon Web Services
people.bio: Has served as CEO Amazon Web Services since June 2024. Previously served as Senior Vice President, Amazon Web Services from February 2021 until June 2024 and held vice president roles in AWS marketing, sales and support, compute services, and EC2.
people.quote: Matthew S. Garman. Mr. Garman has served as CEO Amazon Web Services since June 2024

people.name: Douglas J. Herrington
people.title: CEO Worldwide Amazon Stores
people.bio: Has served as CEO Worldwide Amazon Stores since July 2022. Previously served as Senior Vice President, North America Consumer from January 2015 to July 2022 and held senior vice president and vice president roles in Consumables.
people.quote: Douglas J. Herrington. Mr. Herrington has served as CEO Worldwide Amazon Stores since July 2022

people.name: Brian T. Olsavsky
people.title: Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer
people.bio: Has served as Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer since June 2015. Previously served as Vice President, Finance for the Global Consumer Business from December 2011 to June 2015 and has held financial leadership roles across Amazon since April 2002.
people.quote: Brian T. Olsavsky. Mr. Olsavsky has served as Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer since June 2015

people.name: Shelley L. Reynolds
people.title: Vice President, Worldwide Controller, and Principal Accounting Officer
people.bio: Has served as Vice President, Worldwide Controller, and Principal Accounting Officer since April 2007.
people.quote: Shelley L. Reynolds. Ms. Reynolds has served as Vice President, Worldwide Controller, and Principal Accounting Officer since April 2007.

people.name: David A. Zapolsky
people.title: Senior Vice President, Chief Global Affairs & Legal Officer
people.bio: Has served as Senior Vice President, Chief Global Affairs & Legal Officer since February 2025. Previously served as Senior Vice President, Global Public Policy and General Counsel from May 2023 to February 2025 and held other legal leadership roles dating to April 2002.
people.quote: David A. Zapolsky. Mr. Zapolsky has served as Senior Vice President, Chief Global Affairs & Legal Officer since February 2025.

people.name: Jeffrey P. Bezos
people.title: Chair of the Board
people.bio: Founded Amazon and currently serves as Executive Chair.
people.quote: The Chair of the Board is selected by the Board, and Jeff Bezos, our founder, currently serves as Executive Chair.

people.name: Andrew R. Jassy
people.title: Director and executive officer
people.bio: Serves as a director and executive officer. He receives no additional compensation for his services as a director.
people.quote: Mr. Bezos and Mr. Jassy did not receive any compensation for their services as directors in addition to their compensation for services as executive officers.

people.name: Keith B. Alexander
people.title: Director
people.bio: Serves as an independent director and is not standing for re-election at the Annual Meeting.
people.quote: Gen. Alexander is not standing for re-election at the Annual Meeting.

people.name: Edith W. Cooper
people.title: Director
people.bio: Serves as an independent director and is listed among the director nominees.
people.quote: Ms. Cooper held 4,084 unvested restricted stock units as of December 31, 2025.

people.name: Jamie S. Gorelick
people.title: Lead independent director
people.bio: Serves as lead independent director, presiding over independent-director executive sessions and chairing Board meetings in the Chair's absence.
people.quote: a lead independent director from the Board's independent directors, currently Jamie S. Gorelick, in order to promote independent leadership of the Board.

people.name: Daniel P. Huttenlocher
people.title: Director
people.bio: Serves as an independent director and is listed among the director nominees.
people.quote: Ms. Stonesifer, Dr. Huttenlocher, and Mr. Rubinstein each held 4,695 unvested restricted stock units as of December 31, 2025.

people.name: Andrew Y. Ng
people.title: Director
people.bio: Serves as an independent director and is listed among the director nominees.
people.quote: Dr. Ng held 3,968 unvested restricted stock units as of December 31, 2025.

people.name: Indra K. Nooyi
people.title: Director
people.bio: Serves as an independent director and a member of the Audit Committee.
people.quote: Mrs. Nooyi held 4,806 unvested restricted stock units as of December 31, 2025.

credit.author: JeffBedford from Arlington, Virginia, United States

people.name: Jonathan J. Rubinstein
people.title: Director
people.bio: Serves as an independent director and is listed among the director nominees.
people.quote: Ms. Stonesifer, Dr. Huttenlocher, and Mr. Rubinstein each held 4,695 unvested restricted stock units as of December 31, 2025.

people.name: Brad D. Smith
people.title: Director
people.bio: Serves as an independent director and a member of the Audit Committee.
people.quote: Gen. Alexander and Mr. Smith each held 2,605 unvested restricted stock units as of December 31, 2025.

people.name: Patricia Q. Stonesifer
people.title: Director
people.bio: Served as President and Chief Executive Officer of Martha's Table from April 2013 to March 2019 and interim Chief Executive Officer of The Washington Post from June 2023 to January 2024. Previously held leadership roles at Microsoft and the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation.
people.quote: Ms. Stonesifer served as the interim Chief Executive Officer of The Washington Post from June 2023 to January 2024.

people.name: Wendell P. Weeks
people.title: Director
people.bio: Has served as Corning's Chief Executive Officer since April 2005, Chairman since April 2007, and President since October 2025. Joined Corning in 1983 and held financial, commercial, business development, and general management positions.
people.quote: Mr. Weeks has been the Chief Executive Officer of Corning, a leading glass and materials science innovator, since April 2005
